cuts.raw_narration: Hisoka stands in a bright forest clearing, seen from behind in his sleeveless top marked with a red heart and diamond. He calmly tells Gon he will take his badge back only when Gon can punch him in the face like he just did, and that in the meantime Gon should hold on to it for him — a humiliating so-called return of the badge Hisoka had taken.

The green-capped Amori swaggers up to Killua, who is lying on his back on huge tree roots, and demands the badge, promising he won't get hurt if he cooperates. Killua just mutters 'idiot,' drops down in a blur of motion, and rams a punch into Amori's gut. Amori doubles over gasping while his two brothers rush in, scolding him for going too easy on the squirt.

Killua casually holds up two badges — numbers 197 and 198 — and points out that 198 is only one off from the target he's been hunting, so 199 must be one of them. The middle brother, sweating and stunned, orders the others to get into formation.

The three Amori brothers spread out around Killua in a misty clearing, boasting that no one has ever beaten their formation attack and that they will tear him to shreds. Killua just gives them a mischievous, cat-like smile and replies 'Oh, OK,' then remarks with an eerie glint that his fingers work a lot better than any knife.

Outside a dark cave entrance, Gon insists on going in alone and tells the others that if they don't hear from him in 30 minutes, they should go back to the start. Kurapika refuses point-blank in a tight close-up, declaring that they formed an alliance and he will not abandon Gon. Gon snaps that then the alliance is over — but Kurapika and Leorio calmly reply that they're staying because they want to; it's their choice.

Ponzu explains they're trapped: anyone who tries to leave gets swarmed by snakes — a paralyzing, ultimately fatal trap set by Bourbon, the snake charmer. The camera pans up to reveal a wall of writhing brown and yellow vipers hanging vertically from the ceiling. Kurapika desperately offers Bourbon every badge they have if he'll let them out, but Ponzu just points to a body slumped nearby. In an extreme close-up, Bourbon's shadowed, hooded face with its distinctive square mustache sits perfectly still: he's already dead.
